mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of the natural-person UBO passport or national identity document
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary or competent public authority of the country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Recent utility bill or bank statement for proof of residential address of the UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Utility provider or licensed financial institution
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (or Consular Legalization for non-Hague Convention countries)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of incorporation, registered address, and good standing of a corporate shareholder (if any)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies registry or Chamber of Commerce of the foreign shareholder's jurisdiction

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening against the Spanish national PEP list, SEPBLAC guidance, the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, UN Security Council sanctions, OFAC SDN List, and domestic hate/terrorist financing indicators. Enhanced due diligence required for any PEP, high-risk jurisdiction exposure, or unusual beneficial ownership structure, in accordance with Ley 10/2010 and Circular 1/2017 of Banco de España.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Mercantil Central (RMC) – Certificación Negativa de Denominación Social / CIRCE platform (www.rmc.es and www.circe.es)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names must be written in Latin characters. Spanish and co-official regional languages (Basque, Catalan, Galician) are admissible; foreign-language names must be transliterated into Latin script and may be accepted only if alphabetical characters are used. The legal type designation 'SL' or 'Sociedad Limitada' must be included and must not be substituted with 'SA' or other misleading corporate designators.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection by the Registro Mercantil Central, the applicant may file a new application with alternative names through the RMC telematic channel. If the rejection is believed to be erroneous, the applicant may file an administrative appeal (recurso de alzada) with the Dirección General de Seguridad Jurídica y Fe Pública (Ministry of Justice) within one month of notification, including grounds and supporting evidence. A fresh name reservation, if granted, is valid for 90 days and cannot be formally extended beyond three months.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual office addresses are generally acceptable as the registered office (domicilio social) for an SL in e-commerce, non-regulated toy distribution, and other low-risk sectors, provided that a physical Spanish address is designated for receipt of legal process, registry notifications, and tax/AML inspections. A P.O. Box alone is not permitted as a statutory registered office.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low (approximately 2-5% annual probability of unannounced inspection by the Mercantile Registry, Agencia Tributaria, or SEPBLAC for a low-risk standard business profile)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for low-cost virtual office with mail forwarding and reception

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Royal Legislative Decree 1/2010 of 2 July approving the consolidated text of the Spanish Capital Companies Act (Ley de Sociedades de Capital); particularly Articles 4.2, 22, 25-37, 58-68 and 209.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Mercantil Central for the name certificate; Provincial Mercantile Registry of the registered office address for inscription of the deed.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Public deed of incorporation (escritura de constitución) executed before a Spanish notary and subsequently presented for inscription in the Mercantile Registry.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: The minimum paid-up share capital is EUR 3,000, which must be fully subscribed and paid in cash in the constitution deed. The funds are deposited in a segregated Spanish bank account and may be used only after the company is inscribed in the Mercantile Registry.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the founding quotaholders subscribe fully the EUR 3,000 corporate capital shown in Exhibit A, and that the bank deposit certificate evidencing payment into the segregated escrow account held at the designated credit institution be delivered to the notary prior to execution. RESOLVED, that the registered office is fixed at Calle [Address], Postal Code, Madrid, and shall serve as the legal seat and administrative headquarters for all statutory purposes. RESOLVED, that [Name] is appointed sole administrator (Administrador Único) with the broadest powers under the Capital Companies Act, and is authorised as legal representative before all public registries and authorities. RESOLVED, that the deed be executed, tax registration be obtained, and all necessary municipal and industrial licences be initiated.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Central Mercantile Registry (Registro Mercantil Central) via telematic or in-person request.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit form of denomination certification indicating the proposed exact name 'SL company name' and the ISIC 3240 activity. Wait for the 'Certificación de denominación social' confirming no identical or confusingly similar name exists. The name certificate is valid for three months; reapply if expired.
required_dossiers: Notarial identity documents of each partner
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected due to similarity, submit a new request with an alternative name; no additional administrative fee is charged for the re-application. For unjustified refusal, appeal before the Dirección General de los Registros y del Notariado within one month.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Open Escrow Capital Account and Deposit Capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Authorised Spanish credit institution (bank or savings entity).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a non-interest-bearing escrow account in the name of the future company ('SL in formation'), pay in the full EUR 3,000, and obtain a certificate of deposit (Certificado de depósito) issued by the bank confirming the funds are blocked until registration.
required_dossiers: Passport or residence card (NIE) of each quotaholder
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank refuses the account due to compliance doubts, submit the name certificate and personal documentation to a different supervised credit institution; the deposit certificate may be re-issued.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execute Public Incorporation Deed before Notary
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary public within the territorial district of the planned registered office.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Present the name certificate, deposit certificate, drafted bylaws (estatutos), and identification of all quotaholders to a Spanish notary. The notary supervises the execution of the public deed of incorporation. Simultaneously, the notary requests the NIE numbers for non-resident partners without an NIE.
required_dossiers: Valid passport / NIE of each partner
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary issues a deficiency report (e.g. incomplete AML identification), the partners supply the missing documentation within ten working days. The deed is re-scheduled for the next available notarial slot.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain Provisional Tax Identification Number and Register in the Tax Census
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Spanish State Tax Administration Agency (AEAT) through the territorial delegation or online gateway.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Immediately after the deed is executed, apply for the provisional Corporate Tax Identification Number (NIF CIF provisional) by filing the official form 036 (including the setup of the company's tax domicile) and providing a certified copy of the public deed.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of the incorporation deed
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried, resubmit the deed certification and rectify any mismatch in the registered office address or activity code. Provisional NIF is converted into definitive NIF CIF after registration without additional filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Incorporate by Registration in the Mercantile Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Provincial Mercantile Registry of the registered office.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the notarial deed (first copy), the deposit certificate, and the form 036 acknowledgement (with provisional NIF) to the Provincial Mercantile Registry. The registry examines the deed for legal and statutory validity and issues an inscription entry in the register. Once registered, the SL acquires full legal personality and the provisional NIF becomes definitive.
required_dossiers: Notarial first copy of the public deed
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registrar raises a defect (e.g. incomplete statutory clause), the notary or the administrator files a supplement or rectification deed within two months. In case of formal rejection, the parties may appeal to the Mercantile Registry Directorate within one month; alternatively, the deed is corrected and re-presented.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register the Company with the State and Obtain Definitive NIF
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: AEAT (Central Tax Administration) in coordination with the final Mercantile Registry inscription.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After receiving the certificate of registration from the Mercantile Registry, file form 036 to finalise the definitive NIF and declare the registered address, activity code (ISIC 3240) and applicable tax regime. This updating must be completed within one month following inscription.
required_dossiers: Registration certificate of the Mercantile Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the definitive NIF is not automatically issued, present the registration certificate directly to the provincial AEAT office; file a rectification if the activity code is inconsistent with the deed.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Consejería de Industria of the Autonomous Community (e.g. Consejería de Economía, Industria y Empleo) together with the Municipal City Council (Ayuntamiento) competent for activity licensing.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Licencia de Actividad y Apertura (municipal economic activity licence covering manufacturing, warehousing and storage of non-toxic wooden toys; also known as 'licencia de apertura' or 'licencia ambiental' when environmental assessment is attached).

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministerio para la Transición Ecológica y el Reto Demográfico (national level) and the regional environmental department (Consejería de Medio Ambiente).
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Registration or simplified environmental assessment for minor wood-processing and toy-assembly activities; full EIA report is required only if annual wood processing exceeds 500 tonnes or significant VOC emissions arise.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance with EU Directive 2010/75/EU on industrial emissions for VOC threshold limits (e.g. 50 mg C/Nm³); wastewater discharge must meet local sewer ordinance and Law 7/2022 waste treatment requirements; wood dust exposure limit of 5 mg/m³ TWA; non-toxic finish emissions below occupational exposure limits.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate issued by the technically competent body (OCITE) verifying implementation of the municipal fire protection plan; structural load certificate for the building floor and industrial machinery; occupational health and safety registration under Law 31/1995 and Royal Decree 1215/1997 for workplace storage and machinery safety.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT); official portal: https://sede.agenciatributaria.gob.es
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a newly incorporated Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada (SL), the incorporator must apply for a provisional NIF (Número de Identificación Fiscal) before the notarial deed by filing Modelo 036 (declaración censal) and supporting parent entity documents with AEAT. After registration with the Registro Mercantil, obtain the definitive NIF by submitting the deed and registration certificate. Foreign non-resident shareholders without Spanish ID must obtain an NIE first and may require a fiscal representative. The company must also register for VAT (IVA) on the same Modelo 036 before commencing operations.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation (Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada is a resident capital company taxed under the Impuesto sobre Sociedades at 25% on worldwide income; no pass-through).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box election exists. Spanish corporate tax law provides for: (i) a reduced 15% corporate income tax rate for new companies in the first tax period with a positive tax base and the immediately following period (Art. 29 Ley 27/2014); (ii) election for the consolidated tax regime (Grupo de Consolidación Fiscal) under Art. 58 et seq. Ley 27/2014, when a 70%+ controlling interest exists; (iii) participation exemption regime (ETVE) for qualifying foreign shareholdings; (iv) patent box and R&D relief; (v) mandatory ATAD hybrid mismatch disallowance, not elective. All elections are made via Modelo 036 or the annual corporate income tax return (Modelo 200).

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: IVA (Impuesto sobre el Valor Añadido) — VAT
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No mandatory registration threshold; any person or entity carrying on an economic activity in Spain must obtain a VAT number before beginning operations. For EU distance sellers, the cross-border threshold is EUR 10,000; for the domestic SL, liability commences at the first euro of taxable transactions.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Spain does not operate a continuous transaction control (CTC) system for all taxpayers. The SII (Suministro Inmediato de Información) requires near-real-time invoice reporting via web services/API for large enterprises (annual turnover > EUR 6 million), VAT groups, and entities in the simplified export refund regime. The 'Ley Crea y Crece' mandatorily requires electronic invoicing in B2B transactions and the Verifactu system for invoice verification and QR/stamping, phased in for companies approximately one year from the implementing regulation (expected by 2026). For the current low-turnover SL selling B2C via Amazon/Stripe, standard electronic invoices without SII filing are sufficient, but the taxpayer must issue invoices for B2B customers and retain complete records.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods exported outside the EU are subject to 0% VAT (exempt with credit) under Art. 21 Ley 37/1992 if the goods physically leave EU territory within 90 days of dispatch and the exporter holds documentary proof. Services related to tangible exported goods (e.g., handling, packaging) can also be zero-rated. Intra-EU B2B supplies are exempt with the customer's valid EU VAT number if all conditions of Art. 22 and 26 are met.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Commercial invoice (in Spanish or English) describing the goods as eco-friendly beechwood Montessori toys
Customs Export Declaration (Documento Único Administrativo, DUA – SAD Export), electronically filed via SUMAR/DUA
Bill of Lading or Airway Bill as proof of removal from the EU
Inward Remittance Certificate (bank credit advice) as commercial evidence of payment from the non-resident buyer
Intrastat declaration if intra-EU (threshold applies), and VAT reconciliation report
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: AEAT may audit export zero-rating within the general 4-year prescription period (extended to 10 years for certain cross-border transactions). If documentation is missing or false, the supply will be reclassified as taxable at 21%, with an assessment including late-payment interest (interés de demora) and penalties under Art. 191-193 Ley 58/2003. Penalties range from 50% to 150% of the non-declared amount; fraudulent export claims may be classified as 'infracción grave' or 'muy grave', with surcharges up to 150%, plus clawback of improperly deducted input VAT. If the amount involved exceeds EUR 120,000, criminal liability under the Ley Orgánica 10/1995 may also arise.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de España (Bank of Spain), as Spain's national central bank within the Eurosystem, together with the European Central Bank for euro monetary policy and applicable prudential supervision. Foreign-exchange, foreign-investment, payment-statistics, and capital-movement matters may also involve the Spanish Ministry of Economy, Trade and Enterprise, the Directorate-General for International Trade and Investment, and the State Tax Administration Agency.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Spain uses the euro and operates within the EU single market and the euro-area framework. Current-account transactions, including payments for imports, exports, services, royalties, dividends, interest, and ordinary operating expenses, are generally freely convertible and transferable without a general requirement to obtain prior foreign-exchange approval. Capital-account transactions are also generally liberalized, subject to EU sanctions, anti-money-laundering controls, foreign-investment screening, statistical reporting, beneficial-owner verification, tax compliance, and any sector-specific restrictions. An Spanish Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada may generally receive foreign equity, shareholder loans, and commercial payments and may remit legally distributable profits, dividends, interest, and liquidation proceeds to non-residents. Profit remittance requires adequate distributable reserves, approval of the annual accounts and distribution by the competent corporate body, compliance with creditor-protection and net-equity rules, documentary evidence of the underlying transaction, and applicable Spanish withholding-tax and treaty analysis. Dividend and interest payments to non-residents may require withholding, reporting, and beneficial-owner documentation, with possible relief under an applicable double-tax treaty or EU directive subject to anti-abuse conditions. Banks may delay or reject transfers lacking a clear business purpose, source-of-funds evidence, tax information, or sanctions-screening clearance.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Spain has no general statutory export-proceeds surrender obligation, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no general deadline requiring an exporter to convert foreign-currency receipts into euros. Export proceeds may normally remain in foreign-currency accounts or be converted at the company's discretion. The company must retain commercial invoices, transport and customs evidence, contracts, payment confirmations, and reconciliation records. Banks and payment providers may request transaction-purpose information and may report cross-border payment data or suspicious activity. Statistical, balance-of-payments, foreign-investment, tax, customs, and anti-money-laundering reporting obligations can apply depending on transaction size, counterparty, instrument, and reporting framework; these reporting obligations do not constitute a currency-conversion requirement.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium to High for payment collection, card acquiring, SEPA payments, and marketplace settlements, but not as a complete substitute for a Spanish domestic bank. An EU-authorized electronic-money institution or payment institution may provide services in Spain through passporting, a Spanish branch, or permitted cross-border provision, subject to its authorization scope, safeguarding rules, AML controls, customer due diligence, sanctions screening, transaction limits, and platform risk policies. A non-EU offshore digital EMI cannot lawfully provide regulated payment or e-money services to Spanish customers merely by operating online; it generally requires EU authorization, an authorized EU partner, or an applicable local regulatory basis. EMIs generally do not accept deposits and safeguarded balances are not equivalent to bank deposits or covered by the Spanish Deposit Guarantee Scheme. Stripe and Amazon Pay availability, reserves, settlement timing, rolling holds, chargeback exposure, prohibited-goods rules, and account termination rights must be reviewed separately from the company's bank account.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Spanish law does not impose a universal requirement for all directors to appear physically at a bank branch. Remote onboarding may be available, particularly where the company, directors, beneficial owners, tax identifiers, electronic certificates, and source-of-funds profile are straightforward. The bank may nevertheless require a video interview, certified or apostilled corporate documents, Spanish or sworn translations, NIE or other tax identification, proof of address, proof of operating activity, and an in-person appearance for non-resident directors, complex ownership chains, high-risk countries, cash-intensive activity, unusual funding, or unresolved identity and beneficial-owner issues. The bank's internal policy controls the practical onboarding route.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident shareholder, director, or ultimate beneficial owner with no Spanish tax identification or inconsistent identity data
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Valid passports or national identity documents; NIE or other applicable tax identifiers; recent residential-address evidence; notarized, apostilled, legalized, and sworn-translated documents where required; completed beneficial-owner declaration; ownership chart; director appointment evidence; and a signed explanation of the Spanish business purpose.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opaque ownership chain, nominee arrangements, trusts, or inability to identify the natural-person beneficial owner
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Current registry extracts for every corporate shareholder; constitutional documents; shareholder registers; ownership and control chart through each intermediate entity; trust or foundation documents where relevant; beneficial-owner declarations; board resolutions; and independent corporate-service-provider confirmations.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound capital or shareholder funding inconsistent with the company's size, business plan, or stated source of wealth
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Capital increase or shareholder-loan agreement; corporate approvals; investor bank statements; audited or filed financial statements; tax returns; sale or financing documents evidencing source of wealth; wire-transfer confirmations; a funds-flow diagram; and a written treasury memorandum linking each payment to the approved transaction.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Expected cross-border sales involving Amazon, Stripe, Latin America, high-refund channels, or multiple payment processors
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Business plan; website and marketplace URLs; supplier and customer contracts; payment-processor agreements; product catalogue; shipping and fulfillment arrangements; expected monthly volumes; countries of operation; refund and chargeback controls; VAT and customs registrations; and documented transaction-monitoring procedures.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Toy manufacturing or sale activity with unclear product-safety, import, or licensing compliance
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Product specifications; applicable EU toy-safety conformity assessment; CE-marking records where required; technical file; Declaration of Conformity; EN 71 testing and laboratory reports where applicable; supplier due diligence; timber-origin and sustainability records; packaging and labeling controls; product-liability insurance; and customs classification evidence.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Payments involving sanctioned jurisdictions, sanctioned parties, restricted goods, or unusual intermediaries
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Counterparty identification; sanctions-screening results; end-user and end-use certificates; commercial invoices; transport documents; customs declarations; contract and payment-chain explanation; export-control analysis; screening logs; and legal sign-off for any controlled or elevated-risk transaction.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Frequent cash deposits, personal-account use, unexplained third-party payments, or commingling of company and shareholder funds
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Written treasury policy prohibiting personal-account use; bank reconciliation procedures; approved signatory matrix; invoices and receipts; cash-register records if any; related-party agreements; loan or dividend documentation; and evidence that all company receipts and expenses are routed through corporate accounts.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Tax-residency, VAT, permanent-establishment, or economic-substance uncertainty
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Spanish tax registration; VAT identification; registered-office and operating-location evidence; lease or warehouse agreements; payroll or contractor records; local management evidence; tax-residency certificates where relevant; filing history; and a written analysis of the company's operating model and transfer-pricing position.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Route equity contributions and shareholder loans from the investor's account directly to the Spanish SL's corporate account through SEPA Credit Transfer for euro payments or SWIFT international transfer for non-euro payments. Use the beneficiary's exact legal name, Spanish IBAN, BIC where required, registered address, and a payment narrative identifying the transaction as share capital, capital contribution, or shareholder loan. Spain does not operate a universal foreign-exchange purpose-code system for ordinary corporate wires; the bank may nevertheless require an internal purpose classification, supporting documents, and confirmation of source of funds. Before funding, provide the bank with the deed or corporate resolution approving the capital increase, subscription or loan agreement, ownership records, beneficial-owner information, investor identification, and source-of-funds evidence. Reconcile the incoming payment to the company's ledger and retain the bank advice, accounting entry, corporate filings, and any applicable foreign-investment or statistical declarations. Do not route capital through a director's personal account or an unrelated third-party account.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Use SEPA Credit Transfer or SEPA Instant Credit Transfer for eligible euro-area and SEPA supplier payments, subject to bank limits and sanctions screening. Use SWIFT MT103 or its ISO 20022 equivalent for non-SEPA or non-euro payments, with complete originator, beneficiary, intermediary-bank, invoice, and purpose information. Use commercial documentary letters of credit, standby letters of credit, documentary collections, or bank guarantees for higher-risk suppliers or jurisdictions, subject to UCP 600, ISP98, URC 522, applicable sanctions, and the issuing bank's credit requirements. Match each payment to an approved purchase order, commercial invoice, contract, customs or transport document where applicable, and three-way accounting reconciliation. For imports into Spain, coordinate payment with customs classification, import VAT, EORI information, Incoterms, product-safety records, and freight documentation. Apply segregation of duties, dual approval, beneficiary-change callbacks, sanctions screening, fraud controls, and payment-limit governance.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable foreign-exchange forwards with an authorized bank or regulated investment firm, used to lock exchange rates for documented forecast or committed receipts and payments. Apply MiFID II suitability or appropriateness requirements where applicable, EMIR reporting and risk-mitigation obligations, collateral terms, confirmation controls, and hedge-accounting documentation.

Non-deliverable forwards for currencies with limited convertibility or delivery restrictions, subject to the counterparty's regulatory permissions, local-currency rules, sanctions screening, EMIR obligations, and documented commercial exposure. NDFs are generally unnecessary for ordinary euro-denominated activity and should not be used for speculative trading.

Currency swaps and cross-currency interest-rate swaps with an authorized financial counterparty for recurring or material currency and funding exposures. Document the notional amount, maturity, reset dates, collateral, termination events, valuation, accounting treatment, and underlying exposure.

Foreign-exchange options or collars may be used for material and documented exposures where the company understands premium, strike, settlement, margin, and potential-obligation risks. Avoid leveraged, barrier, or complex structures unless independently approved by the board and supported by a formal risk policy.

Treasury control minimums: board-approved hedging policy; exposure forecast; permitted-counterparty list; transaction-authority matrix; confirmation and independent valuation; collateral monitoring; quarterly effectiveness review; prohibition on speculative positions; and retention of contracts, confirmations, valuations, and accounting records.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Accounts (Cuentas Anuales) – balance sheet, profit and loss account, statement of changes in equity, and explanatory notes, together with audit report where required
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Provincial Mercantile Registry (Registro Mercantil) of the registered office and the Official Gazette (BORME)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For calendar-year accounts: prepare by 31 March; approve at the Annual General Meeting by 30 June; deposit with the Mercantile Registry within one month of approval, i.e. generally by 31 July
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fine of €1,200–€6,000 imposed by the Mercantile Registrar for late filing; closure of the company's registry sheet until accounts are deposited; prolonged non-filing may trigger judicial dissolution if losses reduce equity below one-half of share capital

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate Income Tax Return (Impuesto sobre Sociedades, Modelo 200)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 25 calendar days following the six-month period after the tax year end; for a 31 December year-end, the deadline is 25 July of the following year (or next business day)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing surcharge of 20% if filed within 3 months after the deadline, 10% within 6 months, 5% within 12 months, 2.5% within 18 months; statutory late-payment interest runs from the original date; persistent default enables AEAT embargoes on Spanish bank accounts and assets

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual VAT Summary Return (Resumen Anual de IVA, Modelo 390)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: From 1 to 30 January immediately following the calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late submission fines between €150 and €600 plus a non-filing penalty of up to €2,000; under-declared VAT triggers late-payment interest and may lead to corrective assessments and asset attachment

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Third-Party Operations Report (Declaración de Operaciones con Terceros, Modelo 347)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Between 1 and 20 February of the year following the reporting period; required only if annual transactions with any third party exceed €3,000
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Penalty of €150 per missing or erroneous record, with general fines up to €2,000 when mandatory declarations are not submitted; no administrative strike-off consequence

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A statutory audit is mandatory for an SL of greater scale than the general exemption. The audit is mandatory when, during two consecutive years, the company exceeds at least two of the three thresholds: balance sheet total over €4,000,000; net annual turnover over €8,000,000; average number of employees over 50. Public-interest entities are always audited. Shareholders holding 5% or more of the share capital may also request an audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Código de Comercio (Commercial Code) and the Plan General de Contabilidad (PGC) approved by Royal Decree 1514/2007, as amended; SMEs may use the abbreviated PGC. Consolidated groups of listed companies apply IFRS as adopted by the EU.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Spain does not operate a separate annual UBO renewal form. The SL must maintain the Libro de Titulares Reales (beneficial owners register) and file any update with the Mercantile Registry within one month of any shareholding transfer or change in direct/indirect ownership of 10% or more. The annual deposit of accounts and the shareholder registry provide the implicit annual confirmation of ownership structure for corporate and tax authorities.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (Libro de Registro de Socios)
Single-Member Company Contracts Register (Libro de Contratos con el Socio Único)
Beneficial Owners Register (Libro de Titulares Reales)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 250–650 per year for a compliant registered office service in a major Spanish city (Madrid or Barcelona)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,500–14,000 per year for a standard certified audit by an ICAC-registered auditor, depending on company size, turnover, and consolidated group requirements

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: 15% reduced rate for newly created SLs during the first two tax periods with positive taxable base (Art. 29.1 LIS); 25%/12% tax credits for qualified R&D and technological innovation (Art. 35 LIS); 60% deduction for qualifying intangible income (Patent Box, Art. 23 LIS); €9,000 per worker-year credit for hiring workers with disabilities (Art. 38 LIS); 10%/20% credits for cultural film production (Art. 36 LIS).
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Unlimited (no statutory expiry since fiscal year 2015; offsetting caps of 50%/70% of positive taxable base apply to entities with net turnover ≥ €20M per Art. 26.2 LIS)

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Modelo 200 (declaración del Impuesto sobre Sociedades); mandatory electronic filing through the AEAT Sede Electrónica (sede.agenciatributaria.gob.es), using XML schema of the AEAT; quarterly prepayments on Modelo 202 (standard) or Modelo 222 (large companies with net turnover ≥ €10M)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual (CIT) plus three quarterly prepayment declarations (Modelo 202/222) per fiscal year; tax period generally equals the calendar year but an SL may elect a different fiscal year-end
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 25 calendar days following the six months after the fiscal year-end (i.e., by 25 July for calendar-year companies; the filing window runs from 1 July to 25 July); Modelo 202/222 prepayments due in April (first 20 days), October (1-20), and December (1-20) for calendar-year taxpayers

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxpayer identification data: NIF, corporate name, tax period start and end dates, activity code (CNAE 3240), and the election of accounts in euros
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For the Spanish SL (resident taxpayer), supply the permanent establishment registration if any; non-resident representatives must attach Form 036/037 power-of-attorney data and the tax identification of the ultimate beneficial owner

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting profit or loss before tax as per GAAP (PGC) audited financial statements
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reconcile with local GAAP; foreign-parent adjustments must be documented in the TP file

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Off-balance-sheet adjustments: permanent differences (non-deductible expenses, Art. 15 LIS), temporary differences (impairments, provisions, depreciation), and capital-gain deferrals
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-deductible Spanish withholding borne on inbound dividends/royalties and penalties must be added back

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Positive taxable base after offsetting prior negative tax bases (Art. 26 LIS)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach Form 200 Anexo A (NOL offset working) if NOLs are used

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Modelo 200, Casillas 162-171 (Tipo de gravamen y cuota íntegra)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Application of the 25% statutory rate, or 15% new-entity rate, to the taxable base
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Verify eligibility for the 15% new-entity regime (newly created SL, active commercial activity, not a mere patrimonial holding company)

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax credits for double taxation (international and internal) and incentive credits (R&D, employment, reinvestment)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Support foreign double-tax relief with certificates of tax residency from the source state and TP documentation

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Modelo 200, Casillas 251-258 (Cuota líquida, retenciones, pagos fraccionados y resultado)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net tax liability after prepayments, withholdings, and installments; final amount payable or refundable
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders' withholding (19%) on dividends is independent of the SL's own CIT; the SL must file Form 123 and Form 216 for the withholding

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Modelo 200, Anexo C1 / C2 (Datos de la cuenta de pérdidas y ganancias)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Full P&L data in the standardized breakdown of income and expenses
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Cross-check the P&L against the statutory accounts filed in the Mercantile Registry

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Modelo 200, Anexo D (Documentación de precios de transferencia)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Disclosure of related-party transactions and whether TP documentation (Master/Local File) has been prepared
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Mandatory disclosure of all cross-border related-party transactions even if below the documentation threshold; declare the TP methodology used

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Supplementary box for entity status, tax residence, CFC, DAC6 reportable arrangements (Form D-1), and group entities
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose the ultimate parent (UBO) and any DAC6 (reportable cross-border arrangement) codes

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing without prior AEAT notice: surcharge of 1% per calendar month of delay (max 20%) plus late-payment interest; late filing within 3/6/12 months after deadline triggers surcharges of 15%/20%/25% (Art. 27 LGT). Failure to file: proportional penalty of 50% of the unpaid amount plus fixed €200 per omitted data item (min €300), or fixed €400 when no amount is owed (Art. 198 LGT). Incomplete or incorrect returns: penalty of 15% of the amount not declared (Art. 191 LGT), graduated up to 150% where unlawful concealment exists. Late prepayment (Modelo 202/222): surcharges of 1% per month (max 20%) plus interest; additionally, AEAT may impose a 2% depreciation adjustment? No—keep simple.
